en.title: Central and Peripheral Nervous Systems
en.learning_objective: Trace information through the central nervous system and peripheral nervous system in a simple sensory-response loop.
en.simple_explanation: The central nervous system (CNS) consists of the brain and spinal cord. The peripheral nervous system (PNS) includes nervous tissue outside them and connects the CNS with the rest of the body.
en.how_it_works: Peripheral sensory pathways carry information from the body toward the CNS. Central circuits process that information. Peripheral motor pathways then carry commands from the CNS toward muscles or glands, linking central processing to action.
en.visual:
body stimulus
    ↓  PNS sensory
CNS processing
    ↓  PNS motor
body response
en.use_case: Use this division to localize a problem: ask whether information fails while entering the CNS, during central processing, or while an outgoing command travels through the PNS.
en.expected_result: Given a simple stimulus and response, you can label the body-to-CNS and CNS-to-body parts of the pathway.
en.what_to_notice: CNS and PNS describe connected anatomical regions, not competing systems. Useful behavior depends on information crossing their boundary in both directions.
en.common_mistake: Treating the PNS as input-only. It carries sensory information inward and motor commands outward.
en.practical_tip: Draw the CNS in the center, then add one inward sensory arrow and one outward motor arrow before adding details.
en.question: In a sensory-response loop, what distinct roles do the CNS and PNS play?
en.answer: The PNS carries information between body and CNS; the CNS processes it and organizes responses.
